plain_language_template.PASS: The email metadata is matched to its source email.
plain_language_template.WARN: The source email cannot be identified reliably, so source comparisons are incomplete.
plain_language_template.FAIL: Email Core Fields contradict every possible inspected original or an independently established original source.

utf8_source_header_review.basis: RFC6532 permits direct UTF-8 header values and defines message/global; RFC6531 extends mailbox syntax. Restore valid original UTF-8 bytes from parser surrogate escapes before comparisons, without Unicode normalization or byte changes.
utf8_source_header_review.boundary: Malformed/legacy charset values are not guessed. This is not complete SMTPUTF8/IDNA, normalization or malformed-source diagnostic certification.
utf8_source_header_review.message_global: Recognize registered message/global sources independently of filename extension, including nested-email attachment predicates and original encoded payload extraction.

undecodable_source_header_review.basis: A source comparison needs usable original text. Undecodable mailbox/text octets produce unavailable comparison and VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE, with independent supplied-schema, field-presence and readable-field failures retained.
undecodable_source_header_review.diagnostics: Escape surrogates only in report copies; retained source bytes and internal comparison evidence are unchanged.
undecodable_source_header_review.boundary: No legacy charset guessing, Unicode normalization, general malformed encoded-word recovery or complete source-parser certification.

uninspectable_source_review.basis: Attached originals with no supported matched email summary leave source-header comparisons unavailable and validation incomplete. Extra unrendered originals do not invalidate an independently matched supported email.
uninspectable_source_review.boundary: No new MSG/PST parser or external input inventory is inferred. Isolated omission and container-child checking retain their scopes.

ambiguous_source_header_review.basis: A source owner is not established by fields under test when that tentative source contradicts the record. Check every retained possible original for universal field contradictions or a Core Field tuple that no source can satisfy.
ambiguous_source_header_review.availability: Unknown formats or recovered source header inventories block the universal proof. Per-field unavailable comparisons cannot contribute a definite contradiction. Compatible or unknown candidates retain unassigned ownership and incompleteness. Previously consumed occurrences are not excluded from this proof.
ambiguous_source_header_review.boundary: Bounded by the configured item limit; only established header/size predicates are used. No complete source grammar, charset policy, independent provenance, occurrence assignment or attachment ownership is inferred.

nonsmtp_availability_review.basis: The V61 FOAF decision permits exact raw preservation or an unavailable-normalization outcome for non-SMTP original tokens. Such tokens cannot establish a missing SMTP Agent or a normalized-mailbox count contradiction.
nonsmtp_availability_review.independent_checks: Known SMTP presence, understood known-only mailbox comparisons, supplied FOAF syntax and supplied raw fidelity retain their own predicates. Additional SMTP entries that could derive from non-SMTP tokens require independent normalization evidence.
nonsmtp_availability_review.fallback: Coverage fallback uses only reliably decoded SMTP source agents for mandatory SMTP presence; independent malformed XMP does not invent a source mailbox.
nonsmtp_availability_review.boundary: No directory lookup, invented SMTP mailbox, complete source grammar or complete mixed-address normalization is inferred.

source_scope_coverage_review.basis: EA-PDF source coverage permits independent retained originals and unrendered emails. Source-derived Core Field presence and date conditions follow the selected email original, including a second catalog Source, rather than the first/global original. Unknown ownership stays unavailable; supplied schema and universal contradictions remain independent.
source_scope_coverage_review.boundary: Ordinary raw-address omission is optional and does not become required from an unrelated header. This review does not establish complete source/attachment occurrence ownership, candidate enumeration or source grammar.

nested_source_inventory_review.basis: EA-PDF 7.2 permits original assets containing additional unrendered emails. Known uninspected mail attachments and mailbox envelopes prevent a universal proof based only on outer headers. A scored outer match with a contradicted field remains tentative when these candidates exist.
nested_source_inventory_review.independent_checks: Consistent outer originals remain checkable; ordinary binary attachments do not imply nested email. Supplied schema failures retain their independent predicates.
nested_source_inventory_review.boundary: This guard does not enumerate nested sources, assign nested ownership, parse MSG/PST or certify arbitrary archive contents. Unavailable candidate comparisons remain INCOMPLETE.
nested_source_inventory_review.filename_alternatives: Recognize known uninspected mail candidates through either understood original MIME filename parameter, not only the preferred display name.

downstream_source_binding_review.basis: The metadata pass establishes the pipeline source binding for each email record. Source-fidelity recommendations, ordered header inventories and source-derived native attachment aliases reuse that result, including unassigned ownership. They cannot independently rescore a rejected tentative original.
downstream_source_binding_review.boundary: An unavailable source cannot establish equality, alteration or a source-derived alias checksum. Supplied type errors, known-source recommendation differences and independent native observations retain their predicates. Standalone checks without a pipeline binding retain their documented source-scoring boundary.

utf8_source_header_review.basis: RFC6532 permits direct UTF-8 header values and defines message/global; RFC6531 extends mailbox syntax. Restore valid original UTF-8 bytes from parser surrogate escapes before comparisons, without Unicode normalization or byte changes.

utf8_source_header_review.message_global: Recognize registered message/global sources independently of filename extension, including nested-email attachment predicates and original encoded payload extraction.

undecodable_source_header_review.basis: A source comparison needs usable original text. Undecodable mailbox/text octets produce unavailable comparison and VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE, with independent supplied-schema, field-presence and readable-field failures retained.
undecodable_source_header_review.diagnostics: Escape surrogates only in report copies; retained source bytes and internal comparison evidence are unchanged.
undecodable_source_header_review.boundary: No legacy charset guessing, Unicode normalization, general malformed encoded-word recovery or complete source-parser certification.

uninspectable_source_review.basis: Attached originals with no supported matched email summary leave source-header comparisons unavailable and validation incomplete. Extra unrendered originals do not invalidate an independently matched supported email.
uninspectable_source_review.boundary: No new MSG/PST parser or external input inventory is inferred. Isolated omission and container-child checking retain their scopes.

ambiguous_source_header_review.basis: A source owner is not established by fields under test when that tentative source contradicts the record. Check every retained possible original for universal field contradictions or a Core Field tuple that no source can satisfy.
ambiguous_source_header_review.availability: Unknown formats or recovered source header inventories block the universal proof. Per-field unavailable comparisons cannot contribute a definite contradiction. Compatible or unknown candidates retain unassigned ownership and incompleteness. Previously consumed occurrences are not excluded from this proof.
ambiguous_source_header_review.boundary: Bounded by the configured item limit; only established header/size predicates are used. No complete source grammar, charset policy, independent provenance, occurrence assignment or attachment ownership is inferred.

nonsmtp_availability_review.basis: The V61 FOAF decision permits exact raw preservation or an unavailable-normalization outcome for non-SMTP original tokens. Such tokens cannot establish a missing SMTP Agent or a normalized-mailbox count contradiction.
nonsmtp_availability_review.independent_checks: Known SMTP presence, understood known-only mailbox comparisons, supplied FOAF syntax and supplied raw fidelity retain their own predicates. Additional SMTP entries that could derive from non-SMTP tokens require independent normalization evidence.
nonsmtp_availability_review.fallback: Coverage fallback uses only reliably decoded SMTP source agents for mandatory SMTP presence; independent malformed XMP does not invent a source mailbox.
nonsmtp_availability_review.boundary: No directory lookup, invented SMTP mailbox, complete source grammar or complete mixed-address normalization is inferred.

source_scope_coverage_review.basis: EA-PDF source coverage permits independent retained originals and unrendered emails. Source-derived Core Field presence and date conditions follow the selected email original, including a second catalog Source, rather than the first/global original. Unknown ownership stays unavailable; supplied schema and universal contradictions remain independent.
source_scope_coverage_review.boundary: Ordinary raw-address omission is optional and does not become required from an unrelated header. This review does not establish complete source/attachment occurrence ownership, candidate enumeration or source grammar.

nested_source_inventory_review.basis: EA-PDF 7.2 permits original assets containing additional unrendered emails. Known uninspected mail attachments and mailbox envelopes prevent a universal proof based only on outer headers. A scored outer match with a contradicted field remains tentative when these candidates exist.
nested_source_inventory_review.independent_checks: Consistent outer originals remain checkable; ordinary binary attachments do not imply nested email. Supplied schema failures retain their independent predicates.
nested_source_inventory_review.boundary: This guard does not enumerate nested sources, assign nested ownership, parse MSG/PST or certify arbitrary archive contents. Unavailable candidate comparisons remain INCOMPLETE.
nested_source_inventory_review.filename_alternatives: Recognize known uninspected mail candidates through either understood original MIME filename parameter, not only the preferred display name.

downstream_source_binding_review.basis: The metadata pass establishes the pipeline source binding for each email record. Source-fidelity recommendations, ordered header inventories and source-derived native attachment aliases reuse that result, including unassigned ownership. They cannot independently rescore a rejected tentative original.
downstream_source_binding_review.boundary: An unavailable source cannot establish equality, alteration or a source-derived alias checksum. Supplied type errors, known-source recommendation differences and independent native observations retain their predicates. Standalone checks without a pipeline binding retain their documented source-scoring boundary.

current_rule_text.reexamination_previous_text: Required attachment-record fields and internal owner/stream consistency are distinct from source-dependent fidelity. Original source matching is not a universal mandatory PDF-only rule; isolated sources may be absent and permitted zero-length stored placeholders need not equal the original attachment length. Supplied SizeInBytes and optional CheckSum must agree with associated native stored bytes even without a BodyRendering set or retained source. Differing candidate expectations or stored observations remain unavailable evidence, not proof of consistency. Collection member EA-PDFs are checked recursively in their owning email scope, not against parent attachment records. AFRelationship Alternative identifies a converted representation rather than the native attachment payload (section 7.5). Filename association and available original-source filename comparison preserve exact text, including significant spaces. Stripping path components, control characters or whitespace cannot establish filename equality. MIME parameter values are retained before get_filename() trimming; legal stored aliases remain supported by independent payload evidence. Source-assisted payload association uses the same unique email XMP owner mapping as body routing; similar Message-ID text from another email cannot supply source payload evidence. GUID identity retains priority. Source comparisons treat Table 19 records as unordered: reserve compatible original occurrences across the entire owner-scoped set before diagnostic pairing. Optional checksums and permitted zero-byte placeholders must not consume occurrences needed by other valid records. Equivalent assignments prove field consistency only, not unique occurrence identity. V19 permits byte/media comparisons for multiple candidate attachment records only when their valid size, checksum presence/value and media expectations are equivalent. Every candidate receives the same comparisons; this does not assign an owner or prove unique occurrence identity. Differing expectations remain unavailable, and body ownership checks remain separate. V20: MIME recovery must not fabricate parameter equality. Invalid parameter syntax uses preserved text comparison; malformed source values remain permitted. Source attachment/body summaries retain original Content-Type text and quoted spaces. Legal folding and encoded parameter equivalence remain supported; absent or empty body types retain MIME defaults. V21: Ambiguous association remains unavailable, but a valid supplied SizeInBytes or CheckSum fails when every possible native candidate has a readable contradicting value for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required. Any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Size/checksum observations do not select an owner or occurrence; optional checksum absence, shared streams, zero-byte candidates and Source/Alternative exclusions remain supported. This proves only the reported field contradiction, not inventory completeness or full occurrence consistency. V22: A valid attachment Content-Type or its declared parameters fails when every possible native candidate has an available contradicting reconstruction for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required; any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Parameters are compared independently of the bare media type. Ambiguous parameter comparisons without a proved mismatch remain WARN/unavailable rather than N/A; they cannot hide a separate verified mismatch. MIME recovery safeguards, legal encoded equivalents and exact malformed-text comparisons remain in force. No owner, unique occurrence or complete inventory is inferred.

current_rule_text.spec_excerpt: DPart hierarchy and page relationships follow ISO 32000-2. Optional Type, RecordLevel and NodeNameList retain prescribed types; a supplied RecordLevel identifies an actual zero-based level. The published Table409 correction prohibits DPart Metadata streams. Definite violations fail; unresolved spelling/decoding and bounded traversal remain unavailable. DPartRoot and every DPart node are PDF dictionary objects; a stream with matching entries cannot substitute for one. A leaf requires Start; omitted End defaults to Start for a single-page content set. Single-page leaves omit End.

refinement_2026_10_31.previous_spec_excerpt: Each attachment must have a visible File Attachment annotation within each applicable BodyRendering Content Set. Known absence of all BodyRendering sets is N/A; unresolved body-set applicability is unavailable evidence, not a demonstrated annotation violation. Table 19 preserves the original attachment filename, while the native PDF filename may differ. Declared checksums or uniquely selected source-payload evidence may establish that association; unavailable independent association is not a demonstrated missing-annotation violation. Optional CheckSum presence is not required. Filename equality uses exact decoded filename text, including significant spaces, with UF preferred over F. Filename cleanup is not independent association evidence; permitted renamed payloads still need declared or source-assisted payload evidence. AFRelationship Alternative denotes a converted representation and cannot satisfy the native attachment annotation requirement (section 7.5). A Message-ID-only attachment is first resolved to one email XMP record, preserving identifier case and punctuation, then routed through that email Mail_GUID to DPM body sets. Optional DPM Mail_MessageID presence is not required for this route. A supplied attachment GUID takes priority. Missing or ambiguous XMP owners are unavailable evidence, not demonstrated annotation failures.

V23: Within the existing native-file comparison scope, a normal attachment Content-Type that declares parameters remains unavailable when no native payload association can be established. Another verified attachment does not establish agreement for that record. Report WARN rather than N/A or aggregate PASS; definite mismatches still fail. Do not infer a new native-copy requirement when there are no native files; Source/Alternative exclusions and schema checks remain separate.

A name targets the default PDF 1.7 namespace; a two-item array contains a role name and an indirect target namespace dictionary. Namespace resolution does not replace the separate EA-PDF backward-compatible RoleMap requirements. Standard-only structures continue to omit an unused EA-PDF namespace under the existing local interpretation; section 9.7 does not explicitly state that exemption.

current_rule_text.reexamination_previous_text: Required attachment-record fields and internal owner/stream consistency are distinct from source-dependent fidelity. Original source matching is not a universal mandatory PDF-only rule; isolated sources may be absent and permitted zero-length stored placeholders need not equal the original attachment length. Supplied SizeInBytes and optional CheckSum must agree with associated native stored bytes even without a BodyRendering set or retained source. Differing candidate expectations or stored observations remain unavailable evidence, not proof of consistency. Collection member EA-PDFs are checked recursively in their owning email scope, not against parent attachment records. AFRelationship Alternative identifies a converted representation rather than the native attachment payload (section 7.5). Filename association and available original-source filename comparison preserve exact text, including significant spaces. Stripping path components, control characters or whitespace cannot establish filename equality. MIME parameter values are retained before get_filename() trimming; legal stored aliases remain supported by independent payload evidence. Source-assisted payload association uses the same unique email XMP owner mapping as body routing; similar Message-ID text from another email cannot supply source payload evidence. GUID identity retains priority. Source comparisons treat Table 19 records as unordered: reserve compatible original occurrences across the entire owner-scoped set before diagnostic pairing. Optional checksums and permitted zero-byte placeholders must not consume occurrences needed by other valid records. Equivalent assignments prove field consistency only, not unique occurrence identity. V19 permits byte/media comparisons for multiple candidate attachment records only when their valid size, checksum presence/value and media expectations are equivalent. Every candidate receives the same comparisons; this does not assign an owner or prove unique occurrence identity. Differing expectations remain unavailable, and body ownership checks remain separate. V20: MIME recovery must not fabricate parameter equality. Invalid parameter syntax uses preserved text comparison; malformed source values remain permitted. Source attachment/body summaries retain original Content-Type text and quoted spaces. Legal folding and encoded parameter equivalence remain supported; absent or empty body types retain MIME defaults. V21: Ambiguous association remains unavailable, but a valid supplied SizeInBytes or CheckSum fails when every possible native candidate has a readable contradicting value for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required. Any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Size/checksum observations do not select an owner or occurrence; optional checksum absence, shared streams, zero-byte candidates and Source/Alternative exclusions remain supported. This proves only the reported field contradiction, not inventory completeness or full occurrence consistency. V22: A valid attachment Content-Type or its declared parameters fails when every possible native candidate has an available contradicting reconstruction for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required; any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Parameters are compared independently of the bare media type. Ambiguous parameter comparisons without a proved mismatch remain WARN/unavailable rather than N/A; they cannot hide a separate verified mismatch. MIME recovery safeguards, legal encoded equivalents and exact malformed-text comparisons remain in force. No owner, unique occurrence or complete inventory is inferred.

current_rule_text.reexamination_previous_text: Required attachment-record fields and internal owner/stream consistency are distinct from source-dependent fidelity. Original source matching is not a universal mandatory PDF-only rule; isolated sources may be absent and permitted zero-length stored placeholders need not equal the original attachment length. Supplied SizeInBytes and optional CheckSum must agree with associated native stored bytes even without a BodyRendering set or retained source. Differing candidate expectations or stored observations remain unavailable evidence, not proof of consistency. Collection member EA-PDFs are checked recursively in their owning email scope, not against parent attachment records. AFRelationship Alternative identifies a converted representation rather than the native attachment payload (section 7.5). Filename association and available original-source filename comparison preserve exact text, including significant spaces. Stripping path components, control characters or whitespace cannot establish filename equality. MIME parameter values are retained before get_filename() trimming; legal stored aliases remain supported by independent payload evidence. Source-assisted payload association uses the same unique email XMP owner mapping as body routing; similar Message-ID text from another email cannot supply source payload evidence. GUID identity retains priority. Source comparisons treat Table 19 records as unordered: reserve compatible original occurrences across the entire owner-scoped set before diagnostic pairing. Optional checksums and permitted zero-byte placeholders must not consume occurrences needed by other valid records. Equivalent assignments prove field consistency only, not unique occurrence identity. V19 permits byte/media comparisons for multiple candidate attachment records only when their valid size, checksum presence/value and media expectations are equivalent. Every candidate receives the same comparisons; this does not assign an owner or prove unique occurrence identity. Differing expectations remain unavailable, and body ownership checks remain separate. V20: MIME recovery must not fabricate parameter equality. Invalid parameter syntax uses preserved text comparison; malformed source values remain permitted. Source attachment/body summaries retain original Content-Type text and quoted spaces. Legal folding and encoded parameter equivalence remain supported; absent or empty body types retain MIME defaults. V21: Ambiguous association remains unavailable, but a valid supplied SizeInBytes or CheckSum fails when every possible native candidate has a readable contradicting value for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required. Any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Size/checksum observations do not select an owner or occurrence; optional checksum absence, shared streams, zero-byte candidates and Source/Alternative exclusions remain supported. This proves only the reported field contradiction, not inventory completeness or full occurrence consistency. V22: A valid attachment Content-Type or its declared parameters fails when every possible native candidate has an available contradicting reconstruction for that field. A nonempty candidate set is required; any matching or unreadable candidate blocks that field failure. Parameters are compared independently of the bare media type. Ambiguous parameter comparisons without a proved mismatch remain WARN/unavailable rather than N/A; they cannot hide a separate verified mismatch. MIME recovery safeguards, legal encoded equivalents and exact malformed-text comparisons remain in force. No owner, unique occurrence or complete inventory is inferred.
